notes.lead: How to use the Stress deck
notes.body: Have them say the word before turning the card over, then check. Guessing first is the whole exercise — the default is reliable enough that they should be right most of the time, and being right is what makes the rule stick.

notes.lead: Why these look different from the other decks
notes.body: Everywhere else the pronunciation line respells a word for an English reader — VEE-no, bwon-JOR-no. Here it marks the stressed syllable of the Italian spelling instead, because this deck is about where the stress falls in the written word rather than how the letters sound. Read a-MI-co as the Italian it is: a-MEE-ko.

cards.f: Where does the stress normally fall?
cards.m: On the second-to-last syllable: CA-sa, a-MI-co, spa-GHET-ti. The default is reliable.

cards.f: What does a written accent tell you — città, caffè, perché?
cards.m: That the stress falls on the final syllable. It is marked so you always know.
